headline: NAB's APRA Level 2 (Group) CET1 ratio fell 65 bps in FY25, from 12.35% at 30 Sep 2024 to 11.70% at 30 Sep 2025 (results book capital table, corroborated by the FY21-FY25 trend chart). The bank's stated full-year drivers are lending volume growth, increased long-term investment in the business, and the impact of $0.6bn of shares bought back in FY25 (-15 bps). NAB publishes only a half-on-half (Mar 25→Sep 25) capital walk, not a full-year walk, so only the buyback is quantified in bpts for this comparison; the remaining ~-50 bps is not broken out for FY25 vs FY24. Pro forma CET1 of 11.81% reflects the post-period MLC Life sale.

drivers.narrative: The bank states the impact of $0.6 billion of shares bought back in FY25 was -15 bps. The $3.0bn announced on-market ordinary share buy-back completed on 12 March 2025, cancelling 87.8 million shares, of which $0.6bn was bought back in FY25.

Lending volume growth is a stated key driver of the full-year reduction but is not quantified in bpts for FY25 vs FY24. For context, the half-on-half (Mar 25→Sep 25) walk shows Credit RWA -45 bps (volume -27, asset quality -5, models & methodology -13), driven by business lending growth and RWA overlays on off-balance-sheet exposures.

drivers.bank_label: Increased long term investment in the business
drivers.narrative: The bank cites increased long-term investment in the business as a key driver of the full-year CET1 reduction, but does not quantify its bpts impact for the FY25 vs FY24 comparison.

disagreements.explanation: The task's metric is the APRA Level 2 (Group) CET1 ratio. The Level 1 ratio (L1: 11.60 at Sep 25) and the internationally comparable ratio are different measures and are quoted only as context, never as the movement.

limitations: NAB publishes only a half-on-half (Mar 25→Sep 25) capital walk in both the results book (p30) and investor presentation (p29); no full-year (Sep 24→Sep 25) walk exists. Per method, the half-on-half bars (Cash earnings +82, Dividend -61, Credit RWA -45, Other RWA +1, Other -8) are NOT restated as this comparison's contributions; they are described in the narrative as context for the 2H25 span.

Only the buyback (-15 bps) is quantified in bpts for the FY25 vs FY24 window. Lending volume growth and increased long-term investment are stated as drivers but not quantified in bpts for this comparison, leaving a ~-50 bps residual unquantified.
The -15 bps buyback figure appears only in the results book (single document), capping its confidence at 85.
The half-on-half walk's Credit RWA -45 bps and its sub-parts (volume -27, asset quality -5, models -13) belong to the Mar 25→Sep 25 span, not the FY25 vs FY24 comparison.
Movement endpoints converted from percent (12.35, 11.7) to bps: the unit for this metric is bps.
No published walk covers FY25 vs FY24: the bank's walk for this metric describes another comparison, so the driver split is not walk-verified for this comparison. Confidence is capped at 85.

evidence_records.quote: Group CET1 ratio of 11.70%, down (65 bps) from September 2024. Key drivers of the reduction include lending volume growth, increased long term investment in the business and the impact of $0.6 billion of shares bought back in FY25 (-15 bps)

The Group completed its $3.0 billion announced on-market ordinary share buy-back on 12 March 2025, resulting in the buy-back and cancellation of 87.8 million ordinary shares. $0.6 billion of those shares were bought back in FY25.
